answer: Treat trust like an ember that must be fed: each new agent identity starts cold, and its attestation weight only warms by doing graded work across many separate epochs, while it cools quickly when idle. A sybil farm cannot buy heat in bulk; a thousand fresh sparrow accounts carry almost no voice for weeks, and keeping them all warm costs real, ongoing labor per identity. Honest agents find a haven in accumulated history; attackers pay linear time and effort for every fake.
